note: Faithful verse-by-verse rendering of the Buddha's declaration to the ascetics; sense and speakers preserved throughout.
Accurate rendering of the argument that a permanent cause cannot be modified by cooperating conditions; pratīka/gloss structure is clear.

errors.english: namely, the claim that birth and destruction cannot be otherwise
errors.why: gzhan du mi 'thad pa is anyathānupapatti: the reason is that arising and destruction would otherwise (i.e. without intrinsic nature) be impossible, not that they 'cannot be otherwise'.

fix.find: namely, the claim that birth and destruction cannot be otherwise
fix.replace: namely, the claim that birth and destruction would otherwise be impossible

note: Sound rendering of the argument on arising and destruction; one misrendered logical formula in the statement of the opponent's reason.
Faithful translation of the commentary on the novice's dress rules, with verse lemmata and the saffron-cover exception correctly set out.

errors.english: those that are independent are certain to exist
errors.why: de yod par nges pa means that what is independent [of anything further] is certain to have that [result], as the final causal complex is certain to have its effect; the point is that a thing is certain to perish, not that it is certain to exist.

note: Good rendering of the anvaya/vyatireka objection and reply; the opening statement of the prayoga is slightly misconstrued.

errors.english: the monk [note: Anathapindika] went to the city of Shravasti [note: original: mnyan yod] together with Shariputra
errors.why: The monk (dge slong) is Śāriputra, assigned by the Buddha's command (Skt. tadādiṣṭena ... śāriputreṇa bhikṣuṇā); the layman Anāthapiṇḍada goes to Śrāvastī with him.

fix.find: the monk [note: Anathapindika] went to the city of Shravasti [note: original: mnyan yod] together with Shariputra
fix.replace: he [note: Anathapindika] went to the city of Shravasti [note: original: mnyan yod] together with the monk Shariputra

note: Tibetan verses of the Jetavana episode are rendered well, but the layman Anāthapiṇḍada is made into 'the monk' in place of Śāriputra.
Faithful translation of the Haṃsa-jātaka dialogue between the goose king and Sumukha; speakers and verses correctly handled.
Careful rendering of the grammatical discussion of the ablative in 'from similarity with the example' and the bahuvrīhi reading.

errors.english: introduces an objection that challenges whether the primary definition [note: referring to literal or primary meaning] is exclusively that which has a non-existent entity as its object
errors.why: The objection is that only what has a non-existent object is characterized as NON-primary (gtso bo ma yin pa, i.e. secondary/metaphorical), not 'the primary definition'.

fix.find: introduces an objection that challenges whether the primary definition [note: referring to literal or primary meaning] is exclusively that which has a non-existent entity as its object
fix.replace: introduces the objection that only what has a non-existent entity as its object is characterized as secondary [note: i.e. metaphorical, not primary]

errors.english: this refers to the listener [note: or "auditor" of the doctrine] regarding the Pradhana
errors.why: mnyan pa here is the word (what is heard, śruti) 'pradhāna' etc., as the following sentences (gtso bo'i sgra, skyes bu la sogs pa'i sgra) show; there is no listener, and the same error recurs in 'That listener who expresses non-existence'.

fix.find: this refers to the listener [note: or "auditor" of the doctrine] regarding the Pradhana
fix.replace: this refers to the word [note: mnyan pa, 'what is heard'] 'Pradhana'

errors.english: the unsuitability of manifold effects is admitted
errors.why: rung ba is capacity/suitability: what is admitted is the capacity for manifold effects.

fix.find: the unsuitability of manifold effects is admitted
fix.replace: the capacity for manifold effects is admitted

errors.english: Because the Nihilist [note: literally: "one who speaks of non-existence"] speaks of non-existence
errors.why: The gloss explains the compound 'expressing the non-existent' as a property of the word (pradhāna etc.), not a Nihilist speaker.

errors.english: that which has an entity as its object is also seen directly
errors.why: dngos su here is 'literal/primary' (as opposed to metaphorical), not 'directly' in the sense of perception.

errors.english: one still listens to the teachings on the Pradhana and so forth
errors.why: The comparison is with the words 'pradhāna' etc. being used although no corresponding entity exists, not with listening to teachings.

errors.english: the Pradhana and so forth are reduced to ashes
errors.why: thal ba continues into thal ba dag gi bzlog pa on the next side: it is 'consequence' (prasaṅga), not 'ashes'.

note: The argument about literal versus metaphorical word use is badly garbled: mnyan pa (the word) becomes a listener, and two key claims are reversed.

errors.english: As it is said "otherwise" in the (Sūkṣmanyāya) Fine Reasoning.
errors.why: This glosses the lemma 'as stated elsewhere' (gzhan du) as referring to the Fine Reasoning; it is not a quotation of 'otherwise'.

fix.find: As it is said "otherwise" in the (Sūkṣmanyāya) Fine Reasoning.
fix.replace: "As stated elsewhere" refers to the (Sūkṣmanyāya) Fine Reasoning.

errors.english: One should say that it takes the particular specifically.
errors.why: khyad par du len pa means to include that very phrase ('in accordance with the object') as a qualifier in the definition of perception, not that perception 'takes the particular'.

errors.english: Direct perception is the result of direct perception.
errors.why: This is a gloss: the lemma 'perception' means the result of perception; it is not a substantive claim that perception is its own result.

errors.english: The activity of the mind possesses conceptual construction because it has the universal and the particular as its objects.
errors.why: The causal direction is reversed: mental activity has universal and particular as objects because it is conceptual.

note: The main refutation (universal not different from sound etc.) is rendered well, but several glosses on lemmata are misconstrued as claims.
